description:
Run Python 3.10 against the game: one call made of verb calls. sg.<verb>('what', **options) is the direct call with the same options and reply dicts; per-id whats always answer {results: [...]}.
A script changes nothing unless the run has confirm: true. Seen targets: ids this session's replies showed you (report rows and a finished run's printed or returned value count), int or str constants in the code, selectors in the code (a network, a spread, sg.ref('r7')), what the run builds, and "player". Two routes:
- run_script {code}: a report run. Nothing changes; every target is listed [id or cell, name, current -> new]. To act, send the same code with confirm: true: its rows are now seen.
- run_script {code, confirm: true}: acts as it goes on seen targets. An unseen target stops the run with sg.Stopped (a BaseException); the reply lists that call's targets (now seen), what acted, and the fix.
confirm inside the code is refused.
Saved scripts: write script saves Python under a name, find script lists them, inspect script shows one in full, and run_script {name, args} runs its main(**args). The arguments are checked against main's signature before the run: a missing required argument or an unknown name is a refusal, and a value's type too where the annotation maps one; a list's items and anything else are left to the run. A shared script may hard-code no ids; a world script runs only in the world it was saved in. The journal records the version it ran.
Poll, and put things back:
  sg.write('logic', id=ff, logic='Open', value=1)
  try:
      while sg.read('logic', reads=[{'id': probe, 'atmosphere': True}])['results'][0]['atmosphere']['pressure_kpa'] < 15:
          sg.wait(5)        # poll a sensor with read; a room or find query walks the world
  finally:
      sg.write('logic', id=ff, logic='Open', value=0)   # best effort at session end
  # sure, even at session end: with sg.hold(ff, 'Open', 1, after=0): ...
A confirmed run answers within 30 s, then script-N running (follow with inspect {what: 'job', id}); a report or read-only run waits up to 600 s. sg.help('scripts') has the full API; errors raise sg.Error(code, message, fix, maybe_ran).
Footer: writes by outcome, WARNINGS, CLEANUP, undo script-N, cost.

options.code: Python 3.10 source, run as a function body.
options.name: A saved script to run with args; exactly one of code or name.
options.args: The saved script's main(...) arguments by name; checked before the run.
options.confirm: true: writes act, on seen targets. Left out: a report run; nothing changes.
options.max_wait: How long this reply waits; at most 30 s for a confirmed run.

code.description: Python 3.10 source, run as a function body.

name.description: A saved script to run, with args (find script lists them); exactly one of code or name.

args.description: The saved script's main(...) arguments by name; with name only. A missing required argument or an unknown name is refused before the run; a value's type is checked where main's annotation maps one (int, float, str, bool, list, dict, None), and not further.

confirm.description: true: writes act, on seen targets. Left out: a report run; nothing changes.

max_wait.description: How long this reply waits; a confirmed run answers within 30 s whatever this says (it may only shorten). The run goes on.
